This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in probeOrganizationMember))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67099f21587856ffc8593edacebe35c55b065874` — the merge of head `5cbe099fb1a67fc853a589a98c75572ad39d9a89` into base `d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67099f21587856ffc8593edacebe35c55b065874 && git checkout 67099f21587856ffc8593edacebe35c55b065874
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990 5cbe099fb1a67fc853a589a98c75572ad39d9a89 && git checkout -B drift-repro d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990 && git merge --no-ff 5cbe099fb1a67fc853a589a98c75572ad39d9a89

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d95ddebce912c2bd1ce46f4d46f9bca34bd8b990` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3a152285a2827ced9d754f1450fdbf12ba699387`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/runtime/src/seed-org-scoped-references.integration.test.ts, .changeset/33280-seed-member-probe-bounded.md + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (read only)

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A4 · Fixes #33280 (p3) · narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Read-only: the diff, the head tree, the card thread and the head's check runs, including the Check Changeset job log.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The probe is driven from the member set.** `probeOrganizationMember` (seed-loader.ts ~2913-2974) reads the load organization's `sys_member` rows with `orderBy user_id asc` and `limit 500` (`MEMBER_PROBE_PAGE`, ~3511). It starts with no cursor and then uses `user_id: { $gt: after }`, where `after` is the last id of the previous page. Each non-empty page gets one `sys_user` read with `{ key: value, id: page ids }`, `orderBy id asc`, `limit 1`. No read in the function carries `offset`.
- **The lowest-id rule still holds.** Pages ascend by `user_id`, and members of earlier pages did not match the key. So the first page that answers holds the lowest-id matching member, and the person read takes the lowest id within that page. This is the same answer the old candidate-first probe gave.
- **Page boundaries and ties.** Duplicate `user_id` rows inside one organization cannot occur, because `sys_member` declares a unique `(organization_id, user_id)` index (sys-member.object.ts ~423). Even if they did, `$gt` would skip only further copies of a person who was already asked about. A page is processed before the walk tests whether it ends, so a page of exactly 500 rows is followed by one more read, which comes back empty.
- **NULL `user_id`.** The column is `required: true` (~374-376). Blank values are filtered out of the page anyway (see N1).
- **The read-count bound.** A resolved reference costs one member read and one person read when the organization has fewer than 500 members. A miss costs one more read, `limit 1` on the key alone, which only decides whether the error says "not a member". Neither number depends on how many people in the deployment share the name. The bound pin measures equal counts with 0 and with 120 same-named strangers, on North (hit) and South (miss). It also asserts that no read carries `offset` and that every member read is limited to the load organization.
- **The `id` leg** reads the one membership row (`user_id: value`, `limit 1`) and then the person. A refused member read is still reported on `sys_member`. A non-member id gives `nonMemberMatched: true`, as before.
- **Where the membership check applies.** `judgesInternalIdByMembership` (~4570) is true only when the load has an `organizationId`, is not a dry run, and `probeScopeOf(target).kind === 'members'`. That scope is assigned only to `sys_user` (~3015-3019). Every other target, every load with no organization, and every dry run keeps an id-shaped value verbatim, exactly as before. Non-string values are still kept.
- **Why the dry run is excluded.** A dry run never reads the database (`if (config.dryRun) return { status: 'unresolved' }`), and pass 2 does not run on a dry run (~1234). Including dry runs would report a member's id as unresolved. Excluding them keeps the dry-run verdict as it was.
- **Unchanged behaviour.** A member's id still resolves to itself (pinned both ways). A name or email resolves to the same lowest-id member and is refused with the same "not a member of organization" wording (the #33207 pins and the bound pin). A load with no organization keeps a UUID verbatim (the CONTROL case). An outsider's UUID now leaves the reference empty with the same refusal a name gets (pinned North and South).
- **Ablations.** The PR body reports two: the offset probe restored (the bound pin goes red, 6 vs 2) and the id skip restored (the UUID case goes red). I read these as the author's report and did not re-run them.
- **CI on this head:** 51 check runs, 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed or pending. The 35 include `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `TypeScript Type Check` and `Check Changeset`. `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ② Semver level

- **The arm and its spelling are right: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, not `yes (narrowing)`.** `Clause-②` asks whether the accepted set or the public surface widens. Nothing widens here: no export, schema or route moves. The narrowing arm is right because an outcome that used to land (an outsider's UUID linked) is now refused. The spelling is one of the closed pair, and the title carries `!`, the changeset a `**BREAKING**` banner with its FROM/TO fix.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right, so the level is `patch`.** The protocol kind measures what a metadata author can write. The seed record is authored, but its accepted values do not change. A lookup to `sys_user` takes the same string as before. The same UUID still lands for a member, and on any load with no organization.
- **What moves is a load-time membership check, judged against database state.** It belongs to the services row of `none`. It is the same rule #33207 introduced for names (`.changeset/33207-seed-org-scoped-references.md`: `none`, `patch`). It is the same kind of rule as #33393 (`none`, `patch`).
- **Why not `narrowed`.** `narrowed` would also make `no-migration-prescription` unavailable under the ADR-0087 gate, and would demand a migration-ledger entry. No `migrate meta` conversion can rewrite this value, because the fix (add the membership, or name a member) depends on the target database.
- **The ADR-0087 marker** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` therefore stands. AGENTS.md's Post-Task step 3 says a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. One changeset, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch`, is right.
- **The gate agrees.** Check Changeset passed on this head, and its log reads:
  - `✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition.` / `.changeset/33280-seed-member-probe-bounded.md [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`
  - `✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② no (narrowing) and metadata-protocol none, and it introduces no changeset entry graded minor or above and moves no metadata-protocol baseline — a non-protocol change at patch, its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (if any) untouched by the level.`
- **Keep the check rather than the old skip.** That is the author's choice, and I agree with it (see ④).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tenancy.** The change adds a membership check for id-shaped `sys_user` values on organization-pinned loads. No new grant, no new route, and no other reference target is affected.
- **Other targets keep id-shaped values.** On an organization load, a target with an organization column still keeps a UUID verbatim, as the changeset states. I did not verify whether the engine's write-time reference check judges such an id by organization. That is outside this card.
- **Gate wording.** The Check Changeset log also prints `direction arm: narrowing — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships minor`, from `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1839`. That text disagrees with AGENTS.md, under which a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch`. The script's verdict line accepted `patch`. The wording predates this PR and is not its to fix.
- **Draft.** The PR is a draft. Its author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- N1 (nit): the walk ends on the filtered count (the `memberIds.length` versus `page` test, ~2970), not on the raw row count. A page that carried a blank `user_id` would end the walk early. The schema prevents this today (`user_id` is required), so it is not a defect on this head.
- N2 (nit): no test reaches a second member page (more than 500 members). The bound pin uses an organization with one member, so the `$gt` step and the lowest-id-across-pages argument are unpinned. The same keyset idiom keyed on `id` has driver conformance tests (`resolve-authz-context.ts` ~1224, `*-member-keyset-walk-conformance.test.ts`). This walk is keyed on `user_id`, which those tests do not cover. Candidate for a follow-up card.
- N3 (nit): an id-shaped person value now runs every probe leg (the target field, `name`, then `id`). Only the `id` leg can answer a UUID, but each leg makes a member read, a person read and, on a miss, the wording read. The cost is bounded by the organization, but where it was zero reads it is now several per value. It could go straight to the `id` leg.
- N4 (nit, prose): on an organization load, a UUID that names no person at all is now unresolved and reported, where it used to be kept verbatim. The `Clause-②` line covers this ("resolves only when it names a member"), but the BREAKING paragraph names only the outsider case.
- N5 (nit): because the dry run is excluded, a dry run does not predict the refusal a real load gives an outsider's UUID. The exclusion itself is right (see ①).

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing against `main`.** `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` teaches a natural key, not a UUID, for a reference. Its organization-load table says a `sys_user` reference resolves to a member of the load's organization and never to anyone outside it.
- **It closes the one gap in that rule.** Before this change, an id-shaped value was kept verbatim before any probe, so it was the only way past the documented membership rule. A non-UUID id such as `usr_...` already went through the membership check on the `id` leg.
- **No declared capability is taken away.** No spec key or doc promises that an id-shaped person is kept verbatim. A seed that names a member by id keeps working (pinned), so the narrowing only enforces the rule the docs already state. `Skills-docs: none` holds.
- **The bounded probe is the right shape for a hosted deployment.** There, every organization holds the same seeded names, and the cost now follows the organization's size. Keyset paging also removes the old offset walk's false "not a member" under a concurrent delete.
- **Findings.** Nothing must-fix or should-fix. N1 to N5 are nits that do not affect correctness or the contract.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A4-33280`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`

**VERDICT: PASS**
The declaration (`no (narrowing)`, `none`, `patch`) and the membership check hold at this head. Five nits, none blocking.

- **The narrowing against `main`.** `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` teaches a natural key, not a UUID, for a reference. Its organization-load table says a `sys_user` reference resolves to a member of the load's organization and never to anyone outside it.
- **It closes the one gap in that rule.** Before this change, an id-shaped value was kept verbatim before any probe, so it was the only way past the documented membership rule. A non-UUID id such as `usr_...` already went through the membership check on the `id` leg.
- **No declared capability is taken away.** No spec key or doc promises that an id-shaped person is kept verbatim. A seed that names a member by id keeps working (pinned), so the narrowing only enforces the rule the docs already state. `Skills-docs: none` holds.
- **The bounded probe is the right shape for a hosted deployment.** There, every organization holds the same seeded names, and the cost now follows the organization's size. Keyset paging also removes the old offset walk's false "not a member" under a concurrent delete.
- **Findings.** Nothing must-fix or should-fix. N1 to N5 are nits that do not affect correctness or the contract.
